# requireNull

<link-summary>Returns the value as `null`, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNull() — Returns the value as `null`, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNull(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected null."): null;
```

Strictly `null`. `undefined` is a separate case — `isNil` covers both.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                   | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                     | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected null."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`null` — the same value, typed as `null`.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not `null`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNull(null); // => null
requireNull(undefined); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNull(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
